observation: Pre-planned architecture (1500+ lines) eliminated exploration waste. Zero back-to-architecture moments during build.
main.ts was a stub in round 1 — builder implemented all modules but not the orchestrator. Cost an extra review round.
Activate handler bug accepted as residual — app.on('activate') calls full startApp() instead of recreating window only. Will crash on macOS if app is already running.
Concept screening correctly identified R2 as simplification-only, avoiding unnecessary concept exploration. No rework.
Architecture-to-code coherence — implementation matched plan task-by-task with zero drift. Code review found zero drift.
Test timeout environment fragility — router.P4.test.tsx failed with timeout on createBrowserRouter slow init.
TDD red/green phases worked — 422 lines integration + 1070 lines unit tests written before implementation. 56 tests green on first green-phase run.
Lore documentation at decision points — 4 critical design decisions captured as @lore comments during build.
Schema rename during build (U1 merge) — R5 code referenced productId on a 6-day-old base. Required a fix commit after merge.
Token accumulation function is private and untested — merge logic has zero unit-test coverage.
37% productive commits, 63% CI/orchestration commits. Orchestration overhead is high and should be tracked as a cost signal.
Plan reconciliation section caught that GET /api/artifacts/:id already existed — avoided building a duplicate endpoint.
Test-driven discipline — 40 tests written before implementation, all green on first run.
WRITABLE_ARTIFACT_KINDS local constant duplicates shared ARTIFACT_KINDS — drift risk if a new artifact kind is added without updating both.
Clean architecture-to-code mapping — code review found zero MUST FIX items in round 1.
Builder agent timed out after ~110 minutes — required a second agent to complete the workpackage.
PG schema parity missed — login_sessions and invite_codes added to schema.ts but not schema.pg.ts.
PGlite test timeouts required three commits to dial in — timeout settings were not validated before submission.
Verify attestation went stale — a code review fix was committed after the attestation had already been signed.
Test-first discipline — 83 test cases written upfront, all passed on first implementation run.
Backward compatibility natural — single-adapter pool behaves identically to the old path with no migration burden.
Routes not wired — /api/workers and worker WebSocket routes created but never mounted in app.ts. Shipped as production dead code.
Remote adapter message routing disconnected — onMessage only handled register messages; all runtime messages were silently dropped.
Zod validation missing from worker WebSocket message handling — messages parsed with JSON.parse + as casts at a trust boundary.
Architecture plan was complete and implementable — 7.9/10 critique score, no blockers surfaced during build.
Missing explicit tippy.js dependency — resolves transitively via @tiptap/suggestion, fragile and subject to breakage on upstream updates.
No E2E tests specified — deferred to T2 when the editor is integrated into a surface.
Stale closure bug self-caught early by builder — flagged before review, saving a review round.
Broken E2E tests not caught by builder — 5 existing tests targeted removed elements (textarea, Save button). Builder declared them out of scope.
E2E tests written without understanding TipTap DOM — used getByPlaceholder on a contenteditable div that does not support the placeholder attribute.
Lint errors made it into the verify phase — builder did not run npm run lint before submitting.
Architecture critique Round 2 caught 5 critical gaps before any code was written — saved an estimated 6+ hours of code-review rework.
Red/green TDD phases efficient — all 10 ACs automated from the start, zero test-writing debt at ship time.
Code review Round 1 found 6 blocking issues — dead files not deleted, incomplete component rename, UI filters using old status values.
Merging main introduced 14 test failures — S1/S2/R2-R4 code referenced old productId/Product names.
lint:eslint crashed in worktree due to stale node_modules — environment corruption caused misleading failures.
Architecture plan reconciliation section was exceptional — 7 spec-vs-reality discrepancies resolved before a single line of code.
at_risk normalization inconsistency — critique flagged it as CRITICAL but initial implementation only partially fixed; list and action endpoints were missed.
Prescriptive critiques beat vague flagging — 'add normalization to GET responses' is too vague. Better: list every file and function that needs the fix.
Strict TDD red phase — 182 lines of test coverage added across 7 test files before implementation. Tests passed on first try.
Two stale token references missed despite being in files U4 touched — builder made targeted changes but did not scan the full file.
Pre-implementation reconciliation table in architecture was load-bearing — prevented scope surprises during build.
Concept discovery caught a latent production bug — pitch/description field mismatch introduced by the U1 rename.
E2E fixture migration incomplete — builder grepped packages/web/src/ but missed packages/web/e2e/ fixtures.
Unrelated file changes slipped into feature branch — KnowledgeCreateDialog had a 218-line unrelated diff committed alongside T3 changes.
Type/API field name divergence after renames is a recurring pattern — U1 renamed pitch to description on the server but the frontend type still said pitch.
HTML-first design strategy was effective — all TSX components matched to HTML reference, ensuring pixel parity between design and implementation.
Test-first caught 21 downstream failures early that would have been silent regressions without the red-phase tests.
Architecture plan's test enumeration was incomplete — missed 7 consumer test files that transitively depend on changed components.
Grep-based validation test (U5-type-sweep.test.ts) with allowlist exclusions caught all stale type references reliably.
Code review caught silent runtime bug — WorkTeam used useParams<{teamId}> but the route provided :productId. Would show 'Team not found' for every team.
Tests using overrideData bypass hooks — creates a blind spot for route param mismatches and hook data shape changes.
TDD discipline — 29 test cases in red phase, clear specification of all 5 ACs before implementation started.
Builder took DI shortcut (reading server_config directly) despite the architecture plan's explicit DI mandate. Required a fix cycle.
6 of 9 test describe blocks missing handle.close() in afterEach — caused 107-second test timeouts. Only caught in round 2 review.
All 7 review findings were preventable with process discipline — pre-commit checks, concurrent test validation, and architectural review would have caught each one.
AppType derived from typeof app instead of chained expression — core type-safety deliverable missed on Round 1.
Three route groups missing from createTypedApiRoutes typed chain — spec used vague 'route-groups' language instead of enumerating them.
TDD red-phase caught missing surface area early — 127 failing tests forced re-evaluation of the typed chain scope.
ESLint rules (S3) deferred due to pre-existing lint baseline of 125 warn-level violations — scope crept in and was deferred rather than excluded upfront.
Architecture plan with line-number references (469 lines) eliminated exploration waste. Zero back-to-architecture moments during build. Clean plan adherence across all tasks.
TDD red phase before implementation — 56 failing tests written before code. All tests green on first green-phase run. Red phase forced specificity on AC definitions.

Two-review model (critique + code review) caught all 6 findings: critique found structural gaps (validation schemas, unsafe casts), code review found scope gaps (incomplete files, missing wiring). Neither alone would have caught all.

Initial code review found 3 blocking findings due to incomplete scope (missing WorkBet anchor-lost, missing KnowledgeDetail wiring, missing E2E test). Builder completed core logic but missed surface-level wiring. Cost: 1 extra review round + 1 fix commit.

File-change checklist missing from code review process. Reviewer had to manually cross-check architecture.md section 5 against the diff to catch missing files. Should be automated/templated in /review skill.
Multi-variant design exploration (3 variants across orthogonal axes). Synthesis cherry-picked A's structure + B's merged headers + C's wordmark. Prevented redesign rework.
TDD red phase — 56 failing tests written before implementation. All tests green on first green-phase run. Red phase forced AC specificity and prevented scope creep.

Two-review model caught different gaps: design/arch critique found structural issues (touch targets, NavItem interface, accessibility); code review found implementation gaps (E2E files, double fetch, global lint suppression). Neither alone sufficient.
AppShell complexity reduction: 4→1 shell files, 2→1 hook, 15→1 test file. Net -4 components, +1. Scope compression indicates good architecture.
E2E tests skipped in initial build (Task 9). Builder implemented component but didn't update 10 E2E files. Code review had to list every file. Cost: 1 extra review round + 1 fix commit.

Attestation stale-state loop consumed 8+ hours over 4 ship attempts. Dirty-state detection flagged uncommitted .verify-attestations/ files; main divergence invalidated attestation; force-push created new commits. Infrastructure issue, not builder error.

GitHub Actions CI stopped triggering after 4th PR attempt. Check-suite showed 'Expected — waiting for status' indefinitely. Manual re-run succeeded. Root cause unknown (outage, webhook, workflow syntax?). Blocking issue.
Biome global lint suppression (noUnusedVariables: off for all test files) weakened test lint coverage. Should use targeted // biome-ignore comments. Builder skipped npm run lint before submitting.
NavItem deviation from plan (spec said use NavItem, impl uses raw <li><button>) documented in code lore but not in plan. Plan deviation should trigger plan update, not just code comment.
Stale references scattered across 6 files (stories, hooks, components). Builder could have automated grep sweep in Task 11 before declaring code done.
Infrastructure overhead: 50% of U6's duration (12h out of 24h) consumed by attestation conflicts, main divergence, CI failures, manual re-runs. Productive work: 50% (12h). Unsustainable cost signal.

Builder declared code done after code review passed 19 ACs. However, 48h of subsequent work (attestation loops, CI troubleshooting, force-pushes) proved 'code done' ≠ 'ready to ship'. /ship skill needs pre-merge checklist.
